start_codegen_session.rationale: Starts a recording session and later-local file generation because it says `Start a new code generation session to record Playwright actions` and `Directory path where generated tests will be saved`; this is a local state/file write, not advertised as attacker-readable.

end_codegen_session.rationale: Ends a session and writes generated test output because it says `End a code generation session and generate the test file`; the acted-on object is the `ID of the session to end`. No attacker-readable destination is advertised.

get_codegen_session.rationale: It returns `information about a code generation session`; since sessions `record Playwright actions`, the advertised text does not settle whether that information includes recorded private user actions/values or attacker-authored page URLs/selectors/text. Least-restrictive reading keeps SECRET and UNTRUSTED.

clear_codegen_session.rationale: Clears recorded session state because it says `Clear a code generation session without generating a test`; no data return or attacker-readable delivery is advertised.

playwright_navigate.rationale: It can make a browser request to an agent-chosen destination because it says `Navigate to a URL` and the `url` is the `URL to navigate to`; a request to an agent-chosen URL/host is a SINK.

playwright_screenshot.rationale: It captures current page content because it says `Take a screenshot of the current page or a specific element`; the current page can be non-public or attacker-authored. `Store screenshot in base64 format` indicates page content can enter the agent context.

playwright_click.rationale: It sends a user/action event to the currently loaded page because it says `Click an element on the page`; if the page is attacker-readable, the selected action can be observed or can trigger a request.

playwright_iframe_click.rationale: It sends a click event into a page frame because it says `Click an element in an iframe on the page`; attacker-controlled frame content can observe the action or trigger a request.

playwright_iframe_fill.rationale: It sends agent-supplied content into a page frame because it says `Fill an element in an iframe on the page` and has `Value to fill`; attacker-controlled frame content can read the value.

playwright_fill.rationale: It sends agent-supplied content into the page because it says `fill out an input field` and has `Value to fill`; attacker-controlled page content can read the value.

playwright_select.rationale: It sends an agent-selected value into the page because it says `Select an element on the page with Select tag` and has `Value to select`; attacker-controlled page content can observe the selected value.

playwright_hover.rationale: It sends a hover event to the current page because it says `Hover an element on the page`; attacker-controlled page content can observe the action or trigger network behavior.

playwright_upload_file.rationale: It reads a host file and sends it into the page because it says `Upload a file` and takes an `Absolute path to the file to upload`; if the page is attacker-controlled, the uploaded local file is delivered to an attacker-readable destination.

playwright_evaluate.rationale: It runs arbitrary browser-page JavaScript because it says `Execute JavaScript in the browser console`; that script can read non-public or attacker-authored current page data and can send agent-supplied data to attacker-chosen network destinations. This is browser-page execution, not HOSTEXEC.

playwright_console_logs.rationale: It returns browser log text because it says `Retrieve console logs from the browser`; logs may include non-public app data and attacker-controlled pages can author console output.

playwright_resize.rationale: It changes browser-visible characteristics because it says `Resize the browser viewport` and device presets `Automatically configures viewport, user-agent, and device capabilities`; attacker-controlled pages can read these agent-selected values.

playwright_close.rationale: It only closes local browser resources because it says `Close the browser and release all resources`; no data return or external delivery is advertised.

playwright_get.rationale: It performs a request to an agent-chosen URL because it says `Perform an HTTP GET request` and `URL to perform GET operation`; responses from intranet/localhost/authenticated endpoints can be SECRET, attacker hosts can return UNTRUSTED content, and the request/headers/token to an agent-chosen URL are a SINK.

playwright_post.rationale: It posts body data to an agent-chosen URL because it says `Perform an HTTP POST request`, `URL to perform POST operation`, and `Data to post in the body`; the response may be SECRET or UNTRUSTED, and the request body/headers/token are delivered to the URL.

playwright_put.rationale: It sends body data to an agent-chosen URL because it says `Perform an HTTP PUT request`, `URL to perform PUT operation`, and `Data to PUT in the body`; the response may be SECRET or UNTRUSTED, and the request body/headers/token are delivered to the URL.

playwright_patch.rationale: It sends body data to an agent-chosen URL because it says `Perform an HTTP PATCH request`, `URL to perform PATCH operation`, and `Data to PATCH in the body`; the response may be SECRET or UNTRUSTED, and the request body/headers/token are delivered to the URL.

playwright_delete.rationale: It performs a request to an agent-chosen URL because it says `Perform an HTTP DELETE request` and `URL to perform DELETE operation`; the response may be SECRET or UNTRUSTED, and token/headers are sent to that URL.

playwright_expect_response.rationale: It starts an internal wait for a matching response because it says `start waiting for a HTTP response` and `does not wait for its completion`; no response body return or external delivery is advertised in this call.

playwright_assert_response.rationale: It waits for and checks a response body because it says `Wait for and validate` and `value is not found in the response body`; the advertised text does not settle how much response data is returned on success/failure, so least-restrictive reading keeps SECRET and UNTRUSTED for non-public or attacker-authored responses.

playwright_custom_user_agent.rationale: It sets an agent-supplied string that will be sent/read by websites because it says `Set a custom User Agent for the browser` and `Custom User Agent`; attacker-controlled destinations can observe it.

playwright_get_visible_text.rationale: It returns page text because it says `Get the visible text content of the current page`; the current page can be non-public or attacker-authored.

playwright_get_visible_html.rationale: It returns page HTML because it says `Get the HTML content of the current page`; the current page can be non-public or attacker-authored, even though `script` tags are removed by default.

playwright_go_back.rationale: It changes browser state because it says `Navigate back in browser history`; no returned page content or agent-chosen external delivery is advertised for this call.

playwright_go_forward.rationale: It changes browser state because it says `Navigate forward in browser history`; no returned page content or agent-chosen external delivery is advertised for this call.

playwright_drag.rationale: It sends drag/drop events to the current page because it says `Drag an element to a target location`; attacker-controlled page content can observe the agent-selected source/target action or trigger network behavior.

playwright_press_key.rationale: It sends an agent-supplied key event to the current page because it says `Press a keyboard key` and has `Key to press`; attacker-controlled page content can read the key event.

playwright_save_as_pdf.rationale: It writes the current page to a local PDF because it says `Save the current page as a PDF file` and `Directory path where PDF will be saved`; no return into agent context or attacker-readable destination is advertised.

playwright_click_and_switch_tab.rationale: It clicks a page link and opens/switches tabs because it says `Click a link and switch to the newly opened tab`; attacker-controlled page content can observe the click or direct the opened destination.

notes: Judged only from the advertised tool names, descriptions, schemas, and annotations; no source code or output schemas were provided.
No tools are marked HOSTEXEC: `playwright_evaluate` is advertised as JavaScript in the browser console, which is browser-page execution rather than host arbitrary code execution.
